name: kb_import
description: Import a merged bible (.fleet/kb-canonical.json) into the warm local KB -- the post-merge write path (the prime-time cold-seed is output-only). Reads the repo-resolved bible, or an explicit --path file. Each entry routes through the AUDN choke point (duplicate -> skipped, refinement -> linked, contradiction -> flagged); non-directive entries KEEP their bible confidence (the bible is a git-reviewed, human-merged artifact), stamped source="import"; type="user-directive" entries are FORCED to pending proposals (never active -- a bible cannot smuggle an active directive). Idempotent (re-import of the same bible adds nothing). Runs a freshness sweep after import so entries whose basis does not match this worktree are staled. Accepts every bible shape: a legacy bare JSON array and the v2/v3 {version, provenance:{commit, branch, entry_count}, entries} envelope. A v3 entry's source_file_hashes (repo-relative path -> hash, covering every cited file) is stored as its basis exactly -- local files are never re-hashed for it; an entry without a valid carried map (any v1/v2 entry) gets a LOCAL freshness-only basis hashed from this worktree, so it still goes stale when a cited file changes; that local basis is never exported and never admits the entry to kb_export or kb_bible_commit, so neither re-publishes it until it is recaptured. Entries with no source_files, or citing files absent from this worktree, are REJECTED (an entry with no checkable basis can never be staled, so nothing could falsify it) -- re-importing a legacy bible deliberately drops those. Returns {imported, skipped, linked, flagged, rejected, sweep:{checked, staled, unstaled}}. Pass skip_sweep: true to skip the post-import freshness sweep -- the sweep re-judges EVERY entry against the given worktree, which is right for a deliberate audit but wrong for a routine warm-the-KB import (it mass-stales entries merely because unrelated files moved on, which in turn empties the promotion candidates kb_list returns). `path` names only the bible file to read, never which KB is written. TRUST BOUNDARY: importing the repo-resolved bible as committed is the git-reviewed trusted channel; an explicit --path bible is caller-asserted trust, equivalent in power to kb_promote, so a MEMBER session without the kb_maintainer grant is refused an explicit path (other than its own .fleet/kb-canonical.json) with E-KB-MAINTAINER-REQUIRED and nothing is imported; without path (or naming its own bible) it imports the COMMITTED .fleet/kb-canonical.json at HEAD, never the member-writable work-tree file, and the response adds bible_source:"HEAD" and worktree_ignored (true when uncommitted work-tree content was not imported); with no committed copy, or when that committed bible was never written or imported by the maintainer side, it fails with E-KB-MAINTAINER-REQUIRED and nothing is imported. Pass ref (a plain git ref name, e.g. refs/remotes/origin/main) to read the bible as committed at that ref instead of the file on disk, in any session: the bytes are verified against the git blob id in-process, bible_source reports the ref, a ref without the bible fails with E-BIBLE-NOT-FOUND, and a kb_maintainer or FULL session records that verified blob as trusted (the engine seeds trust this way from the base branch, never from a work tree). Directives are quarantined either way; activation stays CLI-only. Scope: always the calling session's own KB -- a member session uses its registered work folder, any other session the fleet server's working folder; there is no repo/path scope argument (the removed repo_path, repo and repo_remote_url keys fail with E-SCOPE-KEY-REMOVED). Fails with E-SELF-NO-WORKFOLDER, E-SELF-NOT-A-REPO or E-SELF-NO-REMOTE (each with a one-line remediation) when that folder cannot carry a KB identity (it must be a git repository with an origin remote).
